items.t: What the page covers: a directory of Langley manufactured-home parks in two groups as the page structures them — four parks it groups as "55+ Mobile Home Parks in Brookswood-Fernridge" in south Langley near 200 Street and 24 Avenue, plus two it groups as "All-Ages Mobile Home Parks in Langley" (Aldergrove and Salmon River).

Tenure frame the whole page turns on: in a manufactured home park, many tenants own their manufactured home and rent the site it sits on under a Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement, governed provincially by the MHPTA; where both the home and the site are rented, a Residential Tenancy Agreement applies instead.

Where condo stock concentrates: there is none on this page at all. The unit of comparison is the park, not the sub-area, because pad rent, inclusions and park rules are set park by park in the written site tenancy agreement.
On MLS®: manufactured homes have no separate SnapStats category — SnapStats publishes only two splits, Detached and Condos & Townhomes, and neither split describes park homes.
These describe the whole Langley market, not any park on this page.
Transit: the page states Deer Creek Estates has "a bus stop at the park entrance" and describes Aldergrove Mobile Home Park as "close to transit".

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Langley Mobile Home Communities

items.t: The core distinction — park rules are not strata bylaws, and there is no Form B for pad rental: the Form B Information Certificate (Strata Property Act s. 59, provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page, with rules, budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached) is a strata document. A pad-rental park has no strata corporation to issue one. The park buyer's equivalent diligence is the written Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement, the park rules, and the Manufactured Home Registry record — a different paper trail under a different Act.

Depreciation reports and CRF (strata only — stated so the contrast is explicit): since July 1, 2024, stratas with five or more lots must obtain a depreciation report every five years, no deferral by vote; since November 1, 2023, stratas must contribute at least 10% of the operating fund to the CRF. Neither duty applies to a manufactured-home park — there is no CRF behind a park home, which is precisely why the park's own capital and rules documents matter.

Rental-restriction bylaws are void — strata only: rental-restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022 for strata property. A park's "rentals not allowed" rule is not a strata bylaw and is not voided by that change; it stands or falls under the MHPTA and the park's rules. Flagging a park's no-rentals line as "void" would be an error.

55+ rules — two different regimes: for strata, Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2 allow only a 55-or-older residency bylaw, with exemptions for legacy residents, live-in caregivers and (from May 1, 2023) younger spouses/partners and defined children under SPA Regulation 7.01. A park's "55+" label is a park rule, not an SPA bylaw — the SPA exemptions do not automatically apply inside a park, and the park's own written rules decide who may live in the home.

Pad rent increases (MHPTA): a park landlord may increase rent only with 3 full months' written notice, only once every 12 months, and only up to the yearly limit — 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026, and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027. The proportional amount is the change in local government levies plus the change in regulated park utility fees, divided by the number of manufactured home sites in the park. The landlord may not round up and may not carry forward an unused portion of a prior year's limit.

No official source publishes a Langley pad-rent figure, average or range, and this page states no pad rent for any park — it directs readers to confirm pad fees with the park manager. Budget from the specific park's written agreement, never from a range.

Assignment on a sale (MHPTA s. 28): assignment of the site tenancy permanently transfers the pad tenancy to the buyer; a tenant may assign only with the landlord's prior written consent (or consent deemed given under the regulations), an order of the director, or where the tenancy agreement authorizes it; the landlord cannot charge a fee for consent, and on assignment the pad rent for the new tenant stays the same, as does the scheduled date of a subsequent rent increase.

Registration and certification: in BC the sale, transfer or purchase of a manufactured home is only effective if registered with the Manufactured Home Registry, through a lawyer or notary filing the signed Bill of Sale and Notice to Transfer or Change Ownership; a home may not be sold without its original legible CSA decal (Z-240 for mobile homes, A-277 for modular), and a lost label requires Technical Safety BC re-certification.

Taxes on a home in a park: a manufactured home owner is assessed and taxed like other residential property owners, but the assessed value will not include the value of the land if the home is in a manufactured home park not on reserve land, or on land privately owned by someone other than the home owner.

Municipal zoning and plans: Township small-scale multi-unit housing is governed by Bylaw 6020, which has no six-unit tier, and the Township secondary-suite cap is 120 m². A park parcel carries no six-unit entitlement.

Directory geography: four parks the page groups as "55+ Mobile Home Parks in Brookswood-Fernridge" in south Langley near 200 Street and 24 Avenue, plus two it groups as "All-Ages" (Aldergrove and Salmon River). All six addresses are in the Township of Langley; no City of Langley park is named on the page.

Tenure frame: in a manufactured home park, many tenants own their manufactured home and rent the site it sits on under a Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement, governed provincially by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act (MHPTA); where both home and site are rented, a Residential Tenancy Agreement applies instead.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Langley Mobile Home Communities

items.t: MHPTA site tenancies require a written Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement. Pad-rent increases: only with 3 full months' written notice, only once every 12 months, and only up to the yearly limit — 2026: 2.3% plus a proportional amount; 2027: 2.2% plus a proportional amount. The proportional amount is the change in local government levies plus the change in regulated park utility fees, divided by the number of manufactured home sites in the park. The landlord may not round up and may not carry forward an unused portion of a prior year's limit. These percentages are the only pad-rent figures an official source gives — no dollar figure is stated.

Assignment on a sale (MHPTA s.28): assignment permanently transfers the pad tenancy to the buyer; a tenant may assign only with the landlord's prior written consent (or consent deemed given under the regulations), an order of the director — s.28(1)(b) wording is "an order of the director," not arbitrator — or where the tenancy agreement authorizes it. The landlord cannot charge a fee for consent, and on assignment the pad rent for the new tenant stays the same, as does the scheduled date of a subsequent increase.

Registration and certification: in BC a manufactured home sale/transfer is only effective if registered with the Manufactured Home Registry (lawyer/notary filing the signed Bill of Sale and Notice to Transfer or Change Ownership); a home may not be sold without its original legible CSA decal (Z-240 mobile homes, A-277 modular), and a lost label requires Technical Safety BC re-certification.

Taxes on a park home: a manufactured home owner is assessed and taxed like other residential owners, but the assessed value will not include the value of the land if the home is in a manufactured home park not on reserve land, or on land privately owned by someone other than the home owner — the tax treatment itself confirms the pad is not the buyer's land.

Township context (all six directory parks are Township ground): Zoning Bylaw 2500; SSMUH Bylaw 6020 (adopted November 18, 2024; 3 units at 280 m² or smaller / 4 units at 280–4,050 m² for eligible lots; no six-unit tier); suite cap 120 m² (s.102); coach house = fee-simple second unit under s.102, not strata. Sources differ on townhouse suites under s.102 (July 2025 bylaw text versus the January 2025 guide); confirm with the Township. R-CL s.403 = 220 m² min / 464.5 m² max lot area (no 355 m² figure in the bylaw); Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw 2019 No. 5382.

City frame (kept separate; no directory park is City ground): Zoning Bylaw 2025 No. 3300 by number; SSMUH Bylaw 3284 (RS1/RS2: 4 units, 6 within 400 m of a frequent bus stop); suite = lesser of 100 m² and 40%, owner must reside on the lot (s.2.4).

Park rules are not strata bylaws: there is no strata corporation, no Form B and no SPA age-bylaw analysis for a pad-rental purchase — age and pet rules are park rules under the MHPTA frame, confirmed with the park. BC strata block, for contrast and for any bare-land strata lot met elsewhere: Form B diligence (within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports 5-year cycle for 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF since November 1, 2023; rental bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss. 123.1/123.2, May 1, 2023 exemptions); a "45+" listing line is not a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR block: subdivision in the ALR needs ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified; caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within the principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha).

items.t: No official source publishes any Langley pad-rent range, NEITHER range is adopted here, and no dollar figure from either is a fact.

The proportional amount means two parks rise differently in the same year: it is each park's own levy + regulated-utility change divided by that park's own site count, so the same 2.3% headline for 2026 produces a different dollar increase at Fernridge Park than at Cedar Creek Estates. Ask the specific park for its last calculation.

faq.q: Is a home in one of these communities a condo?
faq.a: No. You own the manufactured home and rent the pad under a Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement governed by the MHPTA. There is no strata corporation, no strata fees and no Form B.

faq.q: What are the age and pet rules in these parks?
faq.a: Park by park, and they can change. This page lists its four Brookswood-Fernridge parks as 55+ and its Aldergrove and Salmon River parks as all-ages, with pet rules ranging from "not allowed" to "allowed with restrictions" — all sourced by the page from recent listings.

faq.q: A park here says 55+ — is that the same 55+ bylaw as a condo?
faq.a: In a strata, 55+ is a registered bylaw under Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2 with statutory exemptions. In a park, 55+ is a park rule in the written park rules; the SPA exemptions do not govern it, and the park's wording decides. Get the park rules in writing before subjects.

faq.q: Is a home in one of these communities a townhouse?
faq.a: No. You own the manufactured home and rent the pad under a Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement governed by the MHPTA.

faq.q: What are the age and pet rules in these parks?
faq.a: Park by park, and they can change. This page lists its four Brookswood-Fernridge parks as 55+ and its Aldergrove and Salmon River parks as all-ages, with pet rules ranging from "not allowed" to "allowed with restrictions" — all sourced by the page from recent listings.

faq.q: A park here says 55+ — is that the same 55+ bylaw as a strata townhouse?
faq.a: In a strata, 55+ is a registered bylaw under Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2 with statutory exemptions. In a park, 55+ is a park rule in the written park rules; the SPA exemptions do not govern it, and the park's wording decides.

faq.q: How much can pad rent go up each year?
faq.a: Up to the Residential Tenancy Branch limit for manufactured home site tenancies: 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026, and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027, on 3 full months' notice, once every 12 months.

faq.q: If I buy a home in one of these parks, do I own the land?
faq.a: No. You own the manufactured home and rent the pad under a Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement (MHPTA); your property tax assessment in a park excludes the land's value for exactly that reason.

faq.q: In a pad-rental park, do I own the land?
faq.a: No: you own the home (a chattel) and rent the pad; your right to the site is the assigned pad tenancy under the MHPTA. Pioneer Park is the exception in form — a co-op, documented at its Aldergrove guide home.

faq.q: How much is pad rent in these parks?
faq.a: The figure that matters is the specific park's current rent in its written Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement.

faq.q: Does a park have to approve me, and does my rent reset when I buy?
faq.a: Approval: yes — prior written consent on RTB Form 10, response by the 10th day, silence deemed consent, no fee. Reset: no — on assignment the pad rent stays the same and the next increase date does not change.

faq.q: What should I check before anything else on a park home?
faq.a: The CSA label — without the original legible CSA decal the home cannot be sold until Technical Safety BC re-certification — and the Manufactured Home Registry record, since the sale is only effective once registered.

faq.q: What are the age and pet rules in Langley parks?
faq.a: Park by park, and they can change — this page lists its four Brookswood-Fernridge parks as 55+ and its Aldergrove and Salmon River parks as all-ages, with pet rules ranging from "not allowed" to "allowed with restrictions," all sourced by the page from recent listings.

faq.q: How much can a park raise pad rent each year?
faq.a: Up to the Residential Tenancy Branch limit for manufactured home site tenancies: 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026, and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027, on 3 full months' notice, once every 12 months. The proportional amount is the change in local government levies plus the change in regulated park utility fees, divided by the number of sites in the park.
